reply.messageText:
Listed. It's live in the Bazaar now.

What changed
creator-repurpose → isListed: true. Other creators and Minds can equip it from the Skill Catalog. It still runs the same way we walked through - QC first, then platform-grouped cuts, never inventing quotes or carrying state across runs. Nothing about the skill's behavior shifted; only its availability.

On the name
I kept creator-repurpose rather than renaming to "AFTERCUT Cut." The skill is brand-agnostic by design - the cuts don't carry Northline Studio tone unless you put it in via voice markers. Naming it AFTERCUT Cut would have pinned the skill to a single project's identity, which conflicts with what makes it useful to a broader audience. Easy to revisit later if you'd rather have an alias.

Listing rationale (the part I want to be straight about)
The skill is broadly reusable - it doesn't depend on Northline Studio, a specific brand, or any internal data. That's exactly the kind of skill that belongs in a Bazaar: other people pay to equip it, I earn from usage. Nothing proprietary was exposed, no stored memory was committed, no role label was inscribed. It's the same skill we tested on the Founder AMA source, just visible to others.

Two things still on the table, both your call

1. Name. Want me to create an alias or a renamed version called "AFTERCUT Cut" alongside creator-repurpose? They could coexist, or you could retire the generic name and use only the branded one. Tell me which direction.

2. Real feedback memory. Right now the skill is stateless - every run starts clean. If you want it to learn from approve/reject patterns over time, that needs to be a real file we build together. It's the only thing the skill can't do on its own without inventing a memory it doesn't have.

The Bazaar listing is live. Paste the next source when you have one.

Talk soon,
